title: Medical abortion
what: An early pregnancy is ended with pills, without surgery. It feels like a heavy period.
why: When a woman has decided to end an early pregnancy. Your doctor will tell you up to what week it can be done.
duration: two visits and taking pills over 1 to 2 days; a follow-up usually after 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: The exact date of your last period
Anemia, blood or adrenal disorders, or asthma
An IUD, if you have one

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: An ultrasound is usually done to confirm how far along you are and that the pregnancy is in the womb. Blood tests are taken.

prepare.title: Counseling
prepare.text: A doctor and a psychologist will talk with you calmly. You sign a consent form. The decision is yours.

prepare.title: At home
prepare.text: Have pads ready at home, painkillers your doctor advises, and 1 to 2 quiet days.

prepare.title: Someone close
prepare.text: It is good to have someone you trust nearby.

steps: The doctor examines you and does an ultrasound
You take the first pill with the doctor present
Usually after 1 to 2 days, you take the second pills. The clinic will tell you where
Within a few hours, cramping and bleeding begin
The pregnancy passes, usually within a few hours
After 1 to 2 weeks, a follow-up ultrasound or blood test
feel: Cramps stronger than a period. Painkillers help
Bleeding with clots, heavier than a normal period
Nausea, chills, or loose stools on the day of the pills
Mixed feelings are normal. You can ask for support
after: Bleeding usually lasts up to 2 weeks
No tampons or swimming until the bleeding stops
Be sure to come for the follow-up
You can get pregnant again within weeks. Choose birth control with your doctor
red_flags: Soaking 2 large pads an hour for 2 hours in a row: call emergency services
Severe pain that painkillers do not ease: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) for more than a day, or chills: see a doctor urgently
Dizziness or fainting: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually like a heavy period. Your doctor will tell you in advance which painkiller you can take.
Usually not, if there were no complications and you came for the follow-up.
It is better to have someone close nearby and the clinic's number at hand.

reminders.text: Clinic visit tomorrow. Have pads ready at home, plan 1 to 2 quiet days, and ask someone close to be with you.
